name: Bridge with Semi-Exposed Dummies
description: Bridge with Semi-Exposed Dummies (also known as Honeymoon Bridge variant) is a two-player adaptation of Contract Bridge. It solves the issue of missing players by using two 'Semi-Exposed' hands on the table. Each dummy consists of stacks of cards where only the top card is visible. As cards are played, the hidden cards underneath are revealed. This creates a strategic duel where players must manage their own hand while navigating the unknown elements of the table dummies.

overview.description: Bridge with Semi-Exposed Dummies (also known as Honeymoon Bridge variant) is a two-player adaptation of Contract Bridge. It solves the issue of missing players by using two 'Semi-Exposed' hands on the table. Each dummy consists of stacks of cards where only the top card is visible. As cards are played, the hidden cards underneath are revealed. This creates a strategic duel where players must manage their own hand while navigating the unknown elements of the table dummies.

history.origins: Developed as a 'Honeymoon' Bridge variant to allow two players to enjoy the strategic complexity of Bridge without a full table. It borrows the 'uncovering' mechanic from games like German Whist.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Honeymoon Bridge variants proliferate.
1950s: The semi-exposed dummy format becomes a standard recommendation in Bridge primers for two players.
Present: Popular as a training tool for Bridge players to practice card-reading and deduction.
history.cultural: A staple of the 'Honeymoon' card game sub-genre, emphasizing intimacy and mental rivalry.
history.evolution: The game shifted from simple 'Draw Whist' to this format to better simulate the presence of four hands and the partnership dynamics of standard Bridge.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards in hand. Two dummy hands of 13 cards each are dealt to the table in stacks: 6 face-down cards each covered by a face-up card, with one extra face-up card.

rules.objective: Win enough tricks to fulfill the contract, using both your hand and your designated dummy hand.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid for trumps as in standard Bridge. 2. **Play**: Each turn involves playing two cards—one from the player's hand and one from their dummy. 3. **Uncovering**: When a face-up dummy card is played, the face-down card beneath it is flipped over and becomes available for the next trick.
keyRules: Must follow suit from the specific source hand (Player Hand or Dummy Hand).
The highest card among the four cards played wins the trick for the team.
Standard Bridge bidding and scoring applies.

strategy.basic: Identify the high cards in the dummies early. Use your hand to support your dummy's weak suits and vice-versa.
strategy.intermediate: Deduction: Since you see your hand and the top cards of both dummies, you can calculate the probabilities of hidden cards in the face-down stacks vs. the opponent's hand.
strategy.advanced: Endplay setup: Force the opponent to uncover their dummy cards in a specific order, potentially trapping their high cards under your own established winners.
tips: Don't uncover cards too fast if your hand is weak; you might reveal a high card your opponent can easily capture.
Save your hand's trumps to protect your dummy's high side-suit cards.

variations.name: Full Exposed Dummy
variations.description: All 13 cards of the dummies are dealt face-up immediately, making it a game of perfect information.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes how visible the dummy cards are; the underlying engine phases and actions remain the same.

scoring.description: Standard Bridge scoring with two-player adjustments.
scoring.winCondition: Fulfill the contract or reach target match score.

synthesis.shortDescription: The perfect solution for two Bridge enthusiasts. Manage your own hand while controlling a stacked dummy on the table. Every card played from the dummy reveals a hidden layer of strategy, making this variant a high-skill duel of memory and deduction.
